habit_scope: Radon standpipe in the subslab gravel, capped, preferably stacked through the roof during construction. ORNL §2.2 / Fig 2-5 / Fig 2-6. CMHC Ch2 pipe stub + Ch7 NBC two methods (Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC). Use where there is a reasonable probability radon may be present — contact the state health department (ORNL). Not printed as 'Utah vs Fontana.' Gap gap-P06-fontana-utah-split.
how_it_is_done: ORNL: construction techniques for minimizing radon infiltration 'are appropriate where there is a reasonable probability that radon may be present (see Figure 2-5). To determine this, contact the state health department or environmental protection office.' Check state and local health agencies for need of protection (RADON CONTROL checklist). The potential for radon hazard is present in all buildings (ORNL).

Collection: underslab gravel already in the habit Method. ORNL: 3- or 4-inch diameter PVC, 12-inch section of pipe, inserted vertically into the subslab aggregate and capped at the top. 'A single standpipe is adequate for typical house-size floors with a clean, coarse gravel layer.' Position for easy routing to the roof through plumbing chases, interior walls, or closets. 'It is normally less costly to complete the vent stack routing through the roof during construction than to install or complete the vent stack after the building is finished.' Connecting the vent pipe initially without the fan provides a passive system that may be adequate and can be modified to active later.

ORNL checklist: 'Cast 4-inch-diameter PVC tubing standpipes (capped) into slab.' Lay min 4-in coarse clean gravel. 6-mil poly. Seal joints around pipes. Sump pit with airtight cover; vent sump to outside. Do not use floor drains unless mechanical trap valves are used. Do not install sumps within basements in radon-prone areas unless absolutely necessary.

CMHC Ch2 planning: 'Provide the required pipe stub connection for future radon removal, should radon prove to be a problem after the house is occupied.' Ch7: NBC requires one of two methods — gas-permeable layer with inlet/outlet for depressurization, or 100 mm (4 in) clean granular + pipe at least 100 mm (4 in) through the floor, lower end in the granular, top airtight cap. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. CMHC action level 200 Bq/m3 is Canadian — do not copy as EPA 4 pCi/L; confirm AHJ / health dept.
Still do habit prep: plumbing, gravel, 12-in poly laps, wood out. This is an add where radon is probable, not a skip of poly.
trades: ORNL: construction during slab. CMHC: building owner can test later. No crew size.
tools_equipment: Named: 3- or 4-in PVC standpipe, 12-in section, cap (ORNL). CMHC 100 mm (4 in) pipe — Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
inspection_hold_points: Standpipe in the gravel, capped, before the pour (ORNL).
Poly sealed; penetrations caulked; sump airtight if used (ORNL).
Prefer stack through roof during construction (ORNL). Med confidence as a must — 'normally less costly,' not a code must in ORNL.
when_this_beats_habit: Where state/local health says radon is probable (ORNL). Not printed as Utah-only.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Skipping poly because a pipe is in. Copying CMHC 200 Bq/m3 as a US action level. Inventing Fontana-skip-radon as a book fact (Gap).
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They skip the capped pipe because the slab looks the same without it. ORNL says put it in while the gravel is open.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Radon path on the drawings. Confirm with AHJ / health dept / engineer. Not a stamp. CMHC NBC methods are Canadian — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
risk_if_swapped_late: Retrofit drill-through is possible (ORNL: standpipe can be added by drilling a 4-in hole through the finished slab) but routing the stack later costs more. Catch during construction.
plain_language_summary: If the health department says radon is a live issue, put a capped 3- or 4-inch PVC in the gravel before you pour, and run the stack while the walls are open. Poly still laps 12 inches. CMHC is Canadian. We do not have a book that says Utah yes / Fontana no — that split is a Gap.
spanish_summary: Si salud pública dice radón, ponga PVC de 3 o 4 pulgadas tapado en la grava antes de vaciar, y suba el tubo con las paredes abiertas. El polietileno sigue con 12 pulgadas de traslape. CMHC es canadiense. Utah sí / Fontana no no está en el libro — es Gap.

confidence_notes: ORNL sequence high. Regional Utah/Fontana split not sourced — Gap, med as market. CMHC labeled Canadian. Not in AF&PA or HUD RSDG as a standpipe — already noted on P05 as ORNL-only.
remodel_note: Remodel extras (matching, occupied-site, shoring, demo of an existing house) are not a sequence in CMHC/ORNL/HUD/FM — Gap, do not invent remodel-only methods. Essential Guide is framing-only (opened 2026-08-30; silent on site/layout). B&D Room Additions not used as a P00–P06 sequence.
labor_notes: Crew Gap. No special inspector named.
layering: Gravel (collection) → 6-mil poly → vertical 3- or 4-in PVC 12-in section capped at the slab → optional stack through roof (passive, no fan) → fan later if needed (ORNL).
code_to_check: Contact state health department (ORNL). CMHC NBC radon methods and 200 Bq/m3 are Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Do not invent IRC R-numbers for radon.
time_money: ORNL: stack during construction normally less costly than after finish. Passive first, fan later. No dollars.

walkthroughs.title: American Radon Mitigation stack out the roof
walkthroughs.what_it_shows: Field stack out the roof. Passive/mitigation walkthrough. Confirm AHJ / health dept. Not a Utah-named must in the books.

walkthroughs.what_it_shows: Perforated T under slab, solid stack like plumbing. Field/how-to. Over 90s.

images.caption: ORNL Fig 2-5: radon control — 6-mil poly under slab sealed to wall; sealed penetrations; parge/dampproof; solid drainpipes with mechanical traps. Layer: poly on gravel, sealed to wall. Contact state health dept for need.

ORNL Fig 2-6: soil-gas collection — underslab gravel, standpipe, sealed sump cover, perimeter drain to sump. 3- or 4-in PVC 12-in section capped in the gravel; single standpipe OK on typical house-size floor with clean coarse gravel. Stack through roof during construction if you are going to run it.

inspector_looks_for: Capped 3- or 4-in PVC in the subslab gravel (ORNL). Single standpipe OK on typical house-size floor with clean coarse gravel.
No open floor drain to the gravel without a mechanical trap (ORNL).
inspector_fails: Open floor drains discharging to the gravel without a mechanical trap in a radon-prone basement (ORNL: should be avoided; when used, mechanical trap capable of airtight seal).
do_not_cheap: Capped standpipe in the gravel before the pour (hold).
Poly still 6-mil / 12-in laps (habit layering) — the pipe is not a skip of poly.
Run the stack during construction if you are going to run it — ORNL cost note, not a dollar figure.
smart_save: ORNL: completing the vent stack during construction is normally less costly than after finish. Passive (no fan) first; fan later if tests say so. No dollars.
CMHC: rough-ins not needed for heated crawl spaces without a concrete floor if they remain accessible. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
